arxiv-2412-00975.title: On the Orbital Effects of Stellar Collisions in Galactic Nuclei: Tidal Disruption Events and Ejected Stars
arxiv-2412-00975.creator: Sanaea C. Rose, Brenna Mockler
arxiv-2412-00975.description: Abstract Dense stellar clusters surround the supermassive black holes (SMBH) in galactic nuclei. Interactions within the cluster can alter the stellar orbits, occasionally driving a star into the SMBH’s tidal radius where it becomes ruptured, or expelling a star from the nuclear cluster. This proof-of-concept study examines the orbital effects of stellar collisions using a semi-analytic model.

pmc-12987321.title: Inversion of ϕ-OTDR Spatial Windowing Effects Using Wiener Deconvolution for Improved Acoustic Wavefield Reconstruction
pmc-12987321.creator: Shangming Du, Tianwei Chen, Yuxing Duan, Ke Jiang, Song Wu, Can Guo, Lei Liang
pmc-12987321.description: The spatial response of rectangular pulse heterodyne phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometry (ϕ-OTDR) to an acoustic event is characterized by a windowing function rather than a point-like sensitivity. This effect degrades the system’s spatial resolution and introduces systematic errors in array signal processing. This work presents modeling analysis and a mitigation strategy for this fundamental limitation.

pmc-13095315.title: Extensive peripheral immune cell phenotypes and nephrotic syndrome: Tracing causality through genetics – a bilateral Mendelian randomization study
pmc-13095315.creator: Qiong Liu, Guojun Liang
pmc-13095315.description: Nephrotic syndrome (NS) is a complex renal disorder characterized by significant proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, and hyperlipidemia. While its etiology involves genetic and environmental factors, the role of the immune system in NS’s pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. We adopted a bilateral Mendelian randomization approach, leveraging genetic variations as proxies to explore the causality between immune cell traits and NS.

pmc-13254637.title: First-in-human European experience with novel 22-G end-cutting fine-needle biopsy system: a prospective observational pilot study
pmc-13254637.creator: Dominik Julian van de Loo, Michael Tischendorf, Feras Sanoubara, Dina Khalil, Juliana Stadtmann, Frank Erhard Uschner, Kai Henrik Peiffer, Inga Grünewald, Wim Laleman, Jonel Trebicka, Barbara Braden, Michael Praktiknjo
pmc-13254637.description: Background/AimsEndoscopic ultrasound (EUS)-guided biopsy remains a cornerstone for diagnosing and staging gastrointestinal diseases. Various systems are available, with needle designs for fine-needle aspiration and fine-needle biopsy (FNB) and gauges from 25-G to 19-G. We aimed to report the first European human experience with a novel 22-G end-cutting FNB system (EchoTip ClearCore; Cook Medical).

pmc-13326330.title: Assessing the clinical learning environment among respiratory therapy students in Saudi Arabia: a cross-sectional study
pmc-13326330.creator: Abdulelah M. Aldhahir
pmc-13326330.description: BackgroundThe clinical learning environment plays a critical role in shaping healthcare students’ professional competence, confidence, and readiness for clinical practice. Evaluating students’ perceptions of their clinical training environment can provide valuable insights for improving educational quality and clinical supervision. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical learning environment from the perspective of respiratory therapy (RT) students in Saudi Arabia.

pmc-13574551.creator: Arun Krishnan MP, Nandini Devi R, Praveen K Shenoy, Shoaib Nawaz, Abhilash Menon
pmc-13574551.description: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-based combinations are the current standard first-line treatment for metastatic renal cell carcinoma (mRCC). However, tyrosine kinase inhibitors remain the predominant first-line therapy in many low- and middle-income countries because of limited affordability and access to immunotherapy. Dose reduction of tyrosine kinase inhibitors is frequently practiced in real-world settings to improve tolerability and treatment adherence.

pmc-13601734.title: Comprehensive evaluation of AT(N) imaging biomarkers for predicting cognitive decline
pmc-13601734.creator: Tom Earnest, Braden Yang, Deydeep Kothapalli, for the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, Aristeidis Sotiras
pmc-13601734.description: INTRODUCTIONFew studies have investigated how different Alzheimer's disease biomarker definitions affect predictions of cognitive decline.METHODSWe predicted cognitive decline using 42 biomarker definitions spanning amyloid beta, tau, and neurodegeneration in 383 ADNI participants with baseline neuroimaging and longitudinal cognitive assessments. We identified optimal predictors for each pathology and variable type (continuous, binary, non‐binary categorical) using nested cross‐validation.
